factProposals.value: Weekly email delivery runs on GitHub Actions cron (two schedule entries, 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, to cover both sides of the Central-time DST transition), not Vercel Cron -- no Vercel project has been deployed yet, so GitHub Actions is the only cron target that exists today.

Email delivery goes through Resend, sent from the sandbox address onboarding@resend.dev, which can only deliver to the email address the Resend account itself is registered under until a real domain is verified.

Briefings are generated per company, not globally: briefing_agent.fetch_flagged_hospitals_for_company() joins early_warning_flags to company_hospitals, so a company is only ever briefed on hospitals it actually manages. The prior global design (all nationally-flagged hospitals in one briefing) failed a real live run because Claude could not name all 253 flagged hospitals in a single response.

Idempotency for weekly email sends is enforced by reserving a (company_id, week_of, recipient_email) row via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING before Resend is ever called, not by checking-then-sending. A run triggered twice in the same week sends at most once per operator, verified live by re-running the real job immediately after a successful send.
factProposals.evidence: pipeline/weekly_briefing_email.py (reserve_send_slot); production weekly_briefing_emails table showed exactly 1 row after two consecutive real runs

factProposals.value: No sign-up/auth flow exists yet, so there was nowhere in the schema to look up an operator's real email address. company_members previously stored only a bare user_id with no email column at all.

decisions.statement: Chose GitHub Actions cron over Vercel Cron, despite this story's own task guidance suggesting Vercel.
decisions.rationale: The frontend has never been deployed to Vercel, so there is no Vercel project to attach a scheduled function to. GitHub Actions runs against the repo directly with zero new infrastructure, and is what `.hospulse`'s own more detailed version of this story (STORY-010) already specified.

decisions.statement: Scoped briefings per company rather than raising max_tokens to fit all 253 nationally-flagged hospitals into one oversized global briefing.
decisions.rationale: A single global briefing is not the correct end state for a multi-tenant product regardless of token limits -- a company should only ever see hospitals it manages, the same boundary STORY-006's row-level security already enforces for reads. The token-limit failure surfaced the design gap; fixing the design was the real fix, not a bigger prompt.

decisions.statement: Seeded one real company and one real operator using the user's own email, rather than fabricating a placeholder company or waiting for a real customer sign-up.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wanted nothing fake in this build. A real email that genuinely receives a genuine message is real verification; a placeholder address would not prove the delivery pipeline actually works.
decisions.evidence: production companies/company_members rows; a real Resend provider_message_id recorded against the seeded operator's real email

limitations.statement: Resend's sandbox sender (onboarding@resend.dev) can only deliver to the account's own registered email until a real domain is verified -- this does not yet support sending to arbitrary real customer inboxes.
limitations.evidence: pipeline/weekly_briefing_email.py FROM_ADDRESS; Resend's own sandbox restriction, not something this codebase controls

limitations.statement: A company with no hospitals assigned in company_hospitals (the normal state for any real customer today, since no per-company hospital assignment UI exists yet -- STORY-009, not started) receives no briefing and no email, silently. This is correct behavior, not a bug, but there is no operator-facing signal yet that a company's hospital list is simply empty versus nothing being wrong.
limitations.evidence: pipeline/briefing_agent.py generate_and_save_company_briefing() returns None when fetch_flagged_hospitals_for_company() is empty
